transcript: We've put in the work. Now it's time to get paid. During my first dozen or so hours with Grand Theft Auto 6, I was pretty busy. I fixed my leaky roof, collected some rum from a shady liquor store, played way too many games of pool, and caught a lot of fish. Wow, look at you. I also temporarily borrowed a luxury yacht called Party on the Poop Deck before running it aground and drinking its owner's beer, found a finger in my horniest neighbor's plumbing. Oops, forgot about that. Threatened an alligator wearing a hat. Try and bite me again. See what happens. And got mugged by a drunk sea captain. Here. Before stealing his harpoon gun while he peed in a garden. Over 100 more hours of hijinks later, I've now completely lost track of all the things I've seen and done within GTA 6's astounding open world, and I see no real limit to the amount of time I could spend endlessly exploring Vice City and the massive area around it. Frankly, I've never played anything that's hit quite like GTA 6, and right now, I have zero plans to stop playing it. Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos are an interesting pair of playable characters, and unlike any leads that have come before them in the series. I'll avoid any spoilers in this review, but their priority is really about escape rather than revenge or empire building. You want to get out of here? They’re not angels, and it is invariably their recklessness as small-time crooks that puts them in the wrong place at the wrong time. But the overall sliminess of their far more powerful antagonists does make this couple easy to root for throughout their story, which unfolds like four or five seasons of a prestige TV show. You think he’s yours? No, he couldn’t have. Jason is a capable yet calm and softly spoken army veteran. He remains mostly a mystery throughout, but his quiet cowboy demeanor is not a million miles away from Red Dead Redemption 2’s Arthur Morgan, and I like that. Of all the guys I met around here, you’re the only one who’s not a complete piece of shit. Thanks, man. Lucia, who’s headstrong but not abrasive, and confident but not cocky, gets to showcase a wider range of emotions. She’s easily the most likable and multifaceted woman in the history of the series, and it’s abundantly clear that GTA’s writing has done a huge amount of growing up in the last 13 years. Oh, you idiot. We play mostly as Jason for the opening phase of Chapter One, but that’s a smart way of easing us into the many systems we need to come to grips with. In the time it takes to start and finish many typical shooters and action games, I’d lived several days of a second life as Jason in the relatively quiet tourist town he calls home. Straight away, it’s evident this is not a world of painted-on backdrops and empty props. It feels more lived in and real than anything I’ve ever played, and it’s a world you can interact with at a level never before seen in the series. Yes, it was a long wait, but believe me when I say Rockstar has truly pushed the boat out. Absolutely goddamn right. I'll readily admit that I'm an easy mark for a game like this. I love action movies, car chases, and dad rock, and GTA 6 holds precisely the same things near and dear. I won't discuss the long catalogue of movie references I've spotted, nor any of the specific needle drops Rockstar finds itself indulging in more than ever, one of which has become one of my favorite moments in the entire series. It does take over the dial a bit more than usual for key moments, but it's always to great effect, and it certainly hasn't come at the cost of any reduced focus on radio stations. The mammoth radio track list is absolutely overflowing with solid gold, and just my four favorite stations alone feature nearly 200 songs between them. In a considerable blow to any company trying to sell me a next-generation console in the immediate future, GTA 6 also looks even better than it sounds.
